title: ANDS Studio — Portfolio, registry & correspondence operations
walkthrough:
Every page in this operations layer opens beneath a persistent yellow banner reading "Demo / evaluation environment — nothing here is transmitted to Health Canada and no email is sent. Use it to explore the full workflow safely." The shared top bar shows the brand "ANDS Studio" with a page subtitle (e.g. "· portfolio", "· registry", "· correspondence") and a row of iconified nav chips: "Journey", "Dossiers", "Portfolio", "Registry", "Correspondence" and "Help", plus a user chip at the right. Each nav chip carries a plain-English tooltip (e.g. Portfolio's is "All your dossiers at a glance — progress, blockers and due dates.").

The Portfolio page (subtitle "portfolio") shows an eyebrow "Operations", the heading "Portfolio", and the line "Every product dossier in your organisation — module progress, filing gate and fee status at a glance." In smaller text below: "Every change on this page is captured in the dossier's append-only audit trail — actor and workspace stamped, sequence-numbered, exportable for inspections (open a dossier → Audit)." While data loads the page shows "Loading portfolio…"; with no data it shows "No dossiers yet. Create one in the dossier manager →" (a link to /dossiers). Once dossiers exist, a per-client/sponsor scope selector appears as the first control (defaulting to all sponsors in the workspace), showing the count of dossiers in scope; if the scope has no dossiers the page shows "No dossiers for the selected client / sponsor. Choose a different scope above, or 'All sponsors in this workspace'." A button "Export client status report (CSV)" appears (with the suffix " — this client only" when a specific sponsor is scoped); clicking it downloads portfolio-status.csv (or portfolio-status-{client}.csv when scoped) with columns dossier_id, product, owner, client, soonest_due, submission_type, modules_passed, modules_applicable, filing_gate (READY or "in progress") and fee_status. Three summary cards show large counts labelled "Dossiers", "Ready to file" and "Blocked" (with a "Roll-up for {client} — this client / sponsor only." line above them when a specific sponsor is scoped). If any dossiers have a deadline in the next 30 days (or overdue), a card headed "⏳ {n} dossier(s) with a deadline in the next 30 days" lists them soonest-first, with an "{n} overdue" chip when applicable. The dossier grid sits behind a "Hide/Show dossier grid ({n})" toggle (open by default).

Each dossier row shows its ID, title and submission type (plus "· CS-BE" where applicable); a column of PM metadata reading "Owner {name or —}", "Client {sponsor or —}" (with a shield icon) and "Due {date · label}" (or "none set"); a miniature module tower; and one primary status chip reading "Ready to file", a count like "3/9 modules", or "Blocked" (when the dossier has an open task past due, which outranks the gate). A "Details" expander on each row reveals a fee chip, an NOA clock and collaboration chips. The fee chip renders nothing while loading, then appears as "Fee paid", "Fee waived", "Fee due" with an amount to two decimals and currency (e.g. a figure in CAD), or "Fee —" if unavailable. When the lifecycle service reports a live clock, a chip shows "⏱ NOA: {n}d for brand to act" or "⏱ stay: {n}d remaining", styled as blocked at 10 days or fewer; its tooltip reads, for example, "A Notice of Allegation is served — days left in the brand's 45-day window to start litigation" (an accompanying provenance popover is available). Each row ends with "Open →" and "Viewer" links.

The Registry page (subtitle "registry") shows an eyebrow "Operations" and the heading "Product registry", beside it a shield chip reading "Workspace: {name or 'this client'} · isolated" (tooltip: "You are working inside a single client workspace. Data is walled off per workspace — cross-workspace reads are refused at the API…"), and a toggle button "Register product +" (becoming "Cancel"). Intro text: "Every marketed-product registration — DIN, market status and the post-approval obligations (including Right to Sell) that follow the Notice of Compliance," plus the same audit-trail statement. A "Record only." notice states registering a product or changing its status logs a record in your own workspace and does not transmit or file anything with Health Canada. The form (headed "Register a product") has "Product name" (placeholder "Drugazole 10 mg tablet"), "Dossier ID" (placeholder "e123456"), "DIN (8 digits)" (placeholder "02248808"), "Country" (default "CA") and a "Drug type" select defaulting to "— not set —". Under the DIN field a live line updates as you type: blank shows "Issued by Health Canada at NOC — leave blank until then."; a valid entry shows "✓ Valid DIN format."; anything else shows a count like "✗ A DIN is exactly 8 digits (3/8, digits only)". A note states: "New registrations start as Submitted; move them to NOC-Issued and Marketed as Health Canada progresses. Leave the DIN blank until it is issued with the NOC." The submit button reads "Register product →", changing to "Registering…"; missing fields produce "Product name is required" or "Dossier ID is required", and a bad DIN produces "A DIN is exactly 8 digits (e.g. 02248808)". Registrations load under "Loading registrations…"; with no rows the page says "No registrations yet. Register a product once its dossier reaches NOC." Each registration row offers status transitions; buttons disable while a change saves. When marketable registrations exist, a "Right-to-Sell deadlines" strip appears: "Annual Right-to-Sell fee per marketable DIN — due October 1 of the fiscal year. Amounts are billed by the fees service." Its chips show a product with "due …" while loading, a reason when the fee does not apply, or a line like a product name, DIN in brackets, "due" a date, "FY" a year, and "OVERDUE" in blocked styling when past due (each with a provenance popover). Below sits the "Annual notification checklist — {year}" card: "Tracked on the registry service for this workspace: each tick records who signed it and when, and lands on the audit event stream. (The filings themselves still happen with Health Canada — sources in Help.)" Each ticked item strikes through and shows "✓ signed by {name} · {date time} UTC"; the checkbox disables while the tick saves to the server.

The Correspondence page (subtitle "correspondence") shows an eyebrow "Operations" and the heading "Correspondence & notices": "Log every exchange with Health Canada, ingest notices to drive the DSTS lifecycle, and watch the PM(NOC) statutory clocks on each Form V allegation (a NOA opens the s.6 action window; an s.6 action starts the 24-month stay)," plus the same audit-trail statement. A "Record only." notice states everything on this page logs a record in your own workspace and does not transmit anything to Health Canada — filing with Health Canada happens only through the guided journey's transmit step (CESG). A per-client/sponsor scope selector is the first control (defaulting to all sponsors). An "Open a dossier" card follows with a "Dossier" input (placeholder "e123456") backed by an autocomplete list of in-scope dossiers and an "Open" button (disabled until a valid in-scope ID is entered), and a line "{n} dossier(s) in the current scope. Only these are selectable." Nothing is pre-selected — the filer picks explicitly; until then it shows "Pick a dossier in the selected client / sponsor scope to see its correspondence, notices and NOA clocks." Once a dossier is picked, three sections appear: a notice inbox, the "Correspondence hub", and — behind an "Advanced — Form V / NOA litigation register" expander (subtitled "PM(NOC) allegations & statutory clocks", collapsed by default) — the "Form V / NOA register". The hub shows a record count, an optional client shield chip, a kind filter defaulting to "All kinds" and a "Log correspondence +" button opening a form with Kind, Direction ("Inbound (HC → sponsor)" / "Outbound (sponsor → HC)"), Date, Subject (placeholder "e.g. Response to clarifax on 3.2.P.8 stability"), "HC reference (optional)" (placeholder "e.g. HC6-024-e123456") and "Body / summary (optional)" (placeholder "Key points of the letter…"); "Log record" is disabled until a subject is entered and reads "Logging…" while saving. Empty state: "No correspondence on file yet." Records list kind and direction chips ("HC → sponsor" / "sponsor → HC"), subject, body, reference and date. The NOA register ("File Form V +") explains: "One Form V allegation per patent/CSP on the Patent Register… service opens their 45-day window to sue; a commenced s.6 action triggers the 24-month stay," followed by a "Record only" note that Serve NOA and Record s.6 action log what already happened and do not serve, file or transmit anything. Its create form has "Patent / CSP number", "Allegation" and "Form V date" fields with a "File allegation" button ("Filing…"). Empty state: "No Form V allegations on file. If no patents are listed against the reference product, none are needed." Rows carry status chips such as "Draft — NOA not yet served", "NOA served — 45-day action window open", "s.6 action commenced", "Clear — no s.6 action within 45 days", "24-month stay running" and "Resolved"; live clocks read like "12 days left · 45-day action window ends {date}" and carry a "· calculated aid" caveat plus a provenance popover. Draft rows offer a date input and "Serve NOA" ("Serving…"); served rows add "Court file (optional)" and "Record s.6 action" ("Recording…").
